newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China looks to send advance PLA party to Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: China looks to send advance PLA party to Hong Kong.

text.p: China is looking to send an advance party of up to 300 members of the People's Liberation Army (PLA) to Hong Kong ahead of the handover but will house them in closed camps, Hong Kong media reported on Sunday.

Television and radio reporting from Beijing quoted Cheng Shousan, deputy director of Beijing's Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office, as saying dates and the precise size of the party had to be discussed with Britain.

"Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office deputy director Cheng Shousan said...it was hoped that the advance party of the PLA to be stationed in Hong Kong would come early next year and their number would not exceed 300," Hong Kong's Cable TV said.
Britain hands back Hong Kong, a colony for over a century and a half, to China at midnight on June 30, 1997 when the PLA will replace the British military garrison.
The advance party would include soldiers and support specialists such as medical and communications staff, and would be housed in closed barracks, Cheng was quoted as saying.

The arrival of the PLA is viewed with some trepidation in Hong Kong where the images of troops cracking down on the student-led pro-democracy movement in June 1989 remains branded on the collective memory.

"Cheng Shou-shan, a deputy director in charge of Hong Kong Affairs under the Foreign Ministry, said the standing committee of China's National People's Congress (parliament) would meet in late December to approve a law governing conduct of PLA soldiers in Hong Kong," Radio Hong Kong said.
"He said Beijing would fully consider suggestions on the legislation from Hong Kong people."
Beijing had passed on the draft law to London, Cheung was quoted as saying.
China has pledged that the size of the future PLA garrison would not exceed that of the British garrison at its peak when it numbered about 10,000.
